source_title: Uthappa, T Dilip among four new faces in revamped Mumbai Indians coaching setup - India Today
source_excerpt:
Mumbai Indians have unveiled a revamped coaching group ahead of IPL 2027, appointing four new members under head coach Kieron Pollard. Three former MI players return to the franchise, while T. Dilip joins after his stint with India.
Mumbai Indians have announced a major revamp of their coaching staff ahead of IPL 2027, appointing Robin Uthappa, Mitchell McClenaghan, T. Dilip and Dhawal Kulkarni to key roles. The four will join head coach Kieron Pollard as the five-time champions look to rebuild after missing the playoffs in 2026.
Uthappa has been named batting coach, McClenaghan will oversee the bowling department, Dilip takes charge of fielding, while Kulkarni has been appointed development bowling coach. Three of the four are former MI players, with Uthappa, McClenaghan and Kulkarni returning to the franchise in new capacities.
The appointments follow a series of changes within the backroom staff. Mumbai recently confirmed the departures of bowling coaches Lasith Malinga and Paras Mhambrey, along with fielding coach Carl Hopkinson. These changes came after Mahela Jayawardene stepped down as head coach, with Pollard taking over the top role after previously serving as batting coach. FORMER MI PLAYERS RETURN TO FRANCHISE
Uthappa returns to Mumbai nearly two decades after representing the franchise in the inaugural IPL season in 2008, scoring 320 runs in 14 matches. He later played for Chennai Super Kings in 2021 and 2022, helping them win the title in his first season. The former India batter finished his IPL career with 4,952 runs in 205 matches and won the Orange Cap in 2014 after scoring 660 runs for Kolkata Knight Riders. He was also part of India's 2007 T20 World Cup-winning squad.
McClenaghan was a key member of Mumbai's bowling attack between 2015 and 2019, taking 71 wickets in 56 IPL matches. The New Zealand left-arm pacer was part of three title-winning campaigns as a player, in 2015, 2017 and 2019, and remained part of the wider squad during the 2020 triumph.
Kulkarni, meanwhile, represented MI across two spells between 2008 and 2013 and again from 2020 to 2021. He claimed 86 wickets in 92 IPL matches and was part of the franchise's title-winning squads in 2013 and 2020. His development role will focus on nurturing young Indian bowlers and providing year-round support. T DILIP JOINS AFTER INDIA STINT
Dilip arrives at Mumbai after the BCCI decided not to renew his contract following his tenure with the Indian men's team. His final assignment was the 2025 tour of England. During his time with India, he was part of the coaching setup for the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cup triumphs and the 2025 Champions Trophy victory.
He will now take charge of MI's fielding department, bringing international experience to a coaching group that combines former franchise players with coaches from the national setup. Mumbai will hope the revamped staff can help them return to title contention in IPL 2027. - Ends
